set.st: In 1900 strangers came to Homer, six miles down the river from Winona, looking for money said to have been hidden in one of the caves near Homer by bandits who had held up a train. The man who knew the place was said to be in prison for life and to have told them where it was. Nothing was found. In October 1903 a Homer resident announced a systematic search. A Wisconsin state-news item the next day called it a James boys cache hidden after one of their raids, and said Homer people had taken up the hunt for the third time in three years. The amount is OCR-damaged ("$?,000"). Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself. Mar 1901: two Kentuckians searched Homer caves for $8,500 from a Milwaukee Road train robbery, told by a dying old man; Oct 1903: a Homer resident planned a systematic search for ~$6,000 hidden by train bandits, the one who knew the place being in prison for life. Independent listing: Homer Post Office (historical) [GNIS Post Office, Winona East]; Homer (MN gazetteer 1888: village, pop. 25, 5 listings). This confirms the place existed; the pin position still comes from the earlier source.
